lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: We don't do names up here and we don't do headcounts. You can eat, you can sleep, and if you're counting anybody you can leave.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: Forty of us. Was eleven when I came up. People walk out of Halden with nothing and they get to the third terrace before they stop flinching.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: There's an old woman in the founding charter who kept this place common instead of endowed. Whoever she was, she's the reason there's a gate here and nobody's on it.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: Endowed land, this. There's a trust and a wall and a list of who's entitled. We're on the list. Plenty aren't.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: The vote's this week down there. Won't change anything up here. That's rather the point of up here.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: Word came up that somebody got a clause into the Handover. Forty people cheered at a treaty. I've never seen that before.
